methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Athanor operates in Robotics & Manufacturing, a sector represented by a modest comp universe of one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private peers, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. The company's stage remains undisclosed, as does its current valuation and total capital raised.

The standard peer-median valuation method is not applicable to Athanor. Of the ten same-sector peers identified, none satisfy the filtering criteria for stage alignment or valuation-tier similarity required for a defensible comparable analysis. A same-stage peer set yielded zero matches; an adjacent-stage filter also returned zero; and similar-tier filtering produced zero datapoints. The threshold for peer-median reliability—a minimum of three filtered comparables—was not met. An unfiltered sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity of Robotics & Manufacturing companies across funding stages and business models.

Without sufficient narrow-set triangulation, this analysis cannot generate a specific valuation range. The key uncertainty is stage and current valuation disclosure, which would enable stage-specific peer matching. Once Athanor's funding stage and capital history are clarified, a reanalysis using the five identified private peers as potential anchor points may become feasible. The single public comp offers limited direct guidance absent confirmed stage parity. Any forward valuation must await either disclosure of company metrics or narrowing of the comp set through additional stage-specific data.
